crop.notes: Top half of the article, with headline; it ends mid-sentence ('articles of agreement'), and the rest is in article 297.

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported that after a Bill Davis–Bill Ryall match fell through over money, a match was made in St. Louis between Davis, of California, and Tom Allen, of Cleveland, Ohio, for $1,000 a side.

metadata.notes: Running head reads 'The Missouri Republican--St. Louis, December 5, 1868'. The St. Louis Republic name only dates from 1888.

facts.fact: A match was made in St. Louis between Allen, of Cleveland, Ohio, and Bill (William M.) Davis, the California champion, for $1,000 a side, after a Davis-Ryall match fell through; the terms were debated at Bill Ryall's saloon on Washington Avenue and drawn up at Jack Looney's 'Butcher's Exchange'
places: Bill Ryall's saloon, Washington Avenue, St. Louis
Jack Looney's Butcher's Exchange, St. Louis

notes: Same article as 297 (top half). The Davis-Allen match is the main subject, so focus is primary.
